transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (Aurora CTO), Tom (Aurora NetOps), Priya (Aurora Security), Jamal (Aurora Platform)

Summary (auto): Aurora is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) deployment for in-house inference workloads. Primary concerns: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region constraints, egress controls, KMS integration, and audit logs. They want a technical deep dive and sample network configs; next step is SE deep dive + staging PoC.

00:00 Sofia (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm so glad we could get this on the calendar. quick intro, i'm sofia, account exec, and with me is ethan, our systems engineer, he'll cover the network stuff.
00:18 Lena (Aurora): thanks, sofia. yeah, i'm lena, cto. quick context: we're migrating inference workloads off a managed cloud vendor and want to run Redwood in our VPC for data residency and egress control. we care about latency, and we also have strict audit/KMS requirements.
00:36 Ethan (Redwood): great, nice to meet you all. quick agenda

- understand current infra, network patterns (peering, private endpoints), auth/KMS, and region/residency constraints, then outline options and next steps. sound good?
00:52 Tom (Aurora): sounds good. i'll jump in on network. we run multi-account AWS org, primary region us-east-1, some DR in eu-west-1. our services live in the plat-account and we have cross-account VPC peering for most services.
01:08 Priya (Aurora): and security

we require customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys, we need full audit logs, and SSO via Azure AD SAML. also we want no internet egress from the subnets that touch PHI.
01:26 Ethan: ok that's helpful. two immediate questions

do you prefer VPC peering (IP-level) or private endpoints / PrivateLink? both have tradeoffs around cross-account routing and transitive peering.
01:38 Jamal (Aurora): we currently use VPC peering for most traffic, but we also have a central PrivateLink for some managed services. peering is simpler for low-latency services, but it gets messy with many accounts.
01:54 Sofia: right, and on the redwood side, for our Private product we support both patterns you can deploy a customer-dedicated control plane in our VPC and either peer to your VPC or use AWS PrivateLink endpoints to avoid peering. peering requires route-table updates and possibly shared security controls, PrivateLink keeps traffic endpoint-based.
02:15 Tom: can you do cross-region? we replicate some static models in eu-west but main traffic is us-east.
02:24 Ethan: yes, we can provision dedicated instances in multiple regions; replication is supported. your constraints will determine whether we set up peering in us-east only or provision a regionally colocated stack. keep in mind latency of sync vs cost.
02:40 Lena: our SLA expectations

we want sub-100ms p99 for short text inference internal calls. is that feasible if you're in a peered VPC?
02:52 Ethan: p99 sub-100ms depends on model size and instance type; for smaller models it's possible across a peered VPC in the same AZ. with inter-AZ or cross-region it increases. part of the PoC we'll run benchmarks.
03:10 Tom: what about private endpoints

does your service support VPC endpoints that sit in our account so that nothing traverses the internet?
03:20 Sofia: yes, we support interface endpoints (PrivateLink) and we also offer a managed connector that we can deploy into your account for higher isolation that requires an onboarding process and some infra templating.
03:36 Priya: for KMS, we need Redwood to support customer-managed keys (CMKs)

the keys must never leave our control and should be in our AWS account HSM.
03:46 Ethan: we have integrations for CMKs we can either call your KMS from our control plane over PrivateLink or, for Private/on-prem, we can deploy a control plane in your environment which uses local KMS. need to confirm exact trust model; i'll follow up with a config doc.
04:02 Lena: audit logs

we need request-level logging and retention for 7 years; can logs be forwarded to our S3 bucket or Splunk?
04:12 Sofia: yes, we can stream audit logs to your S3 or to a SIEM via Kinesis/Firehose. we'll include the payload fields we capture; there are redaction options to avoid sensitive content leakage.
04:30 Tom: on routing

if we peer, do you support segmented subnets so we can control which subnets can reach the inference endpoints?
04:39 Ethan: yes, we can publish route tables and you can limit via security groups. note that peering is not transitive; if you have a transit gateway, we can work with that too but that adds config.
04:56 Jamal: we use AWS Transit Gateway for some hubs. any limitations there?
05:04 Ethan: transit gateway works; Redwood can peer via TGW attachments but you need to ensure route propagation and NAT rules are correct. sometimes customers prefer PrivateLink because it avoids TGW complexity.
05:22 Lena: ok, timeline

we want a pilot in 6 weeks if possible. who would own the infra changes?
05:31 Sofia: typically Aurora would provision the peering or PrivateLink in your account, we provide CF/Terraform snippets and the support to validate; our SE (ethan) will run the initial connectivity checks.
05:45 Tom: any firewall/NACL ports to open?
05:49 Ethan: interface endpoints use TLS over standard ports (443). For peering, we use gRPC/tcp on 443 as well for control; for model payloads we stream tokens over HTTP/2. we'll send a minimal list of security group rules.
06:07 Priya: data residency

all token processing must remain in our account/region. do you ever do tokenization or prefetch in other regions?
06:18 Ethan: for Private deployments, processing happens in the deployed control plane; for Hosted we may route to other regions for capacity, but for Private we can pin the stack to your region. we'll note that for the PoC.
06:33 Lena: what about automatic fallback? if a node fails, do you redirect to a hosted instance? we do not want data leaving our VPC in that scenario.
06:43 Sofia: good call our default fallback can be configured; for Private customers with strict residency we disable cross-environment fallback. we can keep failover inside your provisioned capacity or use a read-only degraded mode.
06:58 Tom: how about version pinning and rollouts

we need controlled rollouts of model versions and ability to rollback quickly.
07:08 Ethan: supported. we have rollout policies that can be configured per-route and per-model; for Private you control the deployment window and we can run canaries within your VPC.
07:22 Jamal: curious about metrics and tracing

do you expose per-token latency, token counts, and per-route logs?
07:30 Sofia: yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route latency, and tracing. for Private we can ship a local console or send metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana.
07:44 Priya: SSO

we use Azure AD, SAML SSO is mandatory for our devs.
07:50 Ethan: we support SAML and can federate with your IdP; we will provide metadata files and instructions.
08:02 Lena: ok, open items

we need a network diagram from you, sample terraform for endpoint creation, security guidance for KMS, and a benchmark plan.
08:12 Sofia: noted. ethan will own network diagram + terraform. i'll send pricing + SOW draft.
08:20 Tom: one more

egress controls. If a model needs to pull a remote artifact (e.g., hosted model shard), can we block that?
08:31 Ethan: we can pre-stage model artifacts in your account or in a controlled S3. by default our orchestrator pulls artifacts from S3 endpoints we control, but for Private we can push artifacts into a customer bucket to avoid external pulls.
08:49 Lena: that's critical. we cannot allow any internet retrieval in production.
08:53 Sofia: understood. we'll include pre-staging steps in the onboarding playbook.
09:02 Jamal: how long does onboarding typically take?
09:06 Ethan: for Private (VPC) onboarding it's usually 4-6 weeks including infra changes and a short bench. tighter if you approve infra quickly.
09:18 Priya: what's the billing model for Private

flat monthly reserved or usage hybrid?
09:24 Sofia: both. we offer reserved capacity (monthly commit) with an overage rate and a usage-based option for smaller pilots. we'll send a pricing matrix.
09:35 Tom: any compliance artifacts you can share? SOC2, ISO, and pen test reports?
09:40 Sofia: yes, we will share the security pack and our SOC 2 report; note for Private we can also provide deployment-specific attestation.
09:50 Lena: ok great. next steps?
09:53 Sofia: recap

we'll send network diagram + terraform snippets, security pack, pricing + SOW; schedule the SE deep dive next week, and provision staging PoC.
10:03 Ethan: i'll prepare a connectivity checklist and a sample CloudFormation/Terraform module that creates interface endpoints and route table entries for peering, including examples for Transit Gateway.
10:15 Tom: i'll pull CIDR ranges and talk to infra team about a target subnet and security group constraints, will share by friday.
10:22 Priya: i'll review KMS requirements and send any regulatory docs.
10:27 Sofia: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll capture these as action items in the follow-up.
10:34 Lena: thanks, bye.
